newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P places Sydkraft on creditWatch.
newsitem.headline: S&P places Sydkraft on creditWatch.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's on Wednesday placed Swedish power utility Sydkraft on creditwatch with negative implications and affirmed its domestic short-term rating at K-1.
The action followed Sydkraft's announcement on Tuesday that it was buying 12.5 percent of German's Hamburgische Elektricitats-Werke (HEW) for about 650 million marks from the City of Hamburg.
S&P said this affected about $130 million of rated debt.
"The HEW investment may negatively effect Sydkraft's cash flow and financial flexibility," S&P said in a statement.
It said the purchase was likely to be financed with cash although details had not yet been finalised.
If debt-financed cash flow net interest coverage fell slightly below three times, net leverage could increase to 58 percent from 51 percent, S&P said.
"The effect of the investment on Sydkraft's financial profile will hence be relatively moderate and a rating change, if any, would be modest," S&P said.
German PreussenElektra, which is Sydkraft's largest single shareholder, has also acquired 12.5 percent of HEW this week.
But S&P said it would take some years before full operational benefits were obtained as deregulation of the German electricity market was likely to be a gradual process.
